seo.title: Washing Dogs in a Shelter or Rescue: Products That Turn Over
seo.description: Shelters and rescues wash many animals with limited staff and limited time. Which pet care formats suit high-turnover use, and what to order for a shelter.

faq.q: What is the fastest way to wash a newly arrived dog?
faq.a: A no-rinse foam. It needs no bath, no drying setup and no rinse step, which removes most of the labour from the process. It is a spot clean rather than a full bath, so a dirty or matted animal still needs a proper wash, but for an intake line where animals arrive one after another it is the format that scales.

faq.q: Is a no-rinse foam safe for cats and small breeds?
faq.a: The 200 mL paw format suits smaller animals and is designed for paws after walks rather than whole-body use. For a cat or small dog arriving in intake, the 300 mL no-rinse foam is the practical size for a full spot clean.

faq.q: Can shelters buy in smaller quantities?
faq.a: The standard minimum is 2,000 bottles per SKU across the grooming line. Shelters typically order through a distributor or a regional NGO buyer rather than direct, because the volume a single shelter can absorb rarely reaches the factory minimum. We work with resellers who serve this channel.

faq.q: What documentation do we need for donor reporting?
faq.a: Every consignment includes a batch certificate of analysis and a 16-language safety data sheet, which are the documents a procurement audit normally asks for. Certificates of origin and the commercial invoice carry the HS code for customs.

body.html:
Intake washing is a different problem from home bathing. The constraint is not the animal's coat — it is staff time. A shelter processing twenty arrivals a week does not need a luxury bath; it needs the shortest procedure that leaves the animal clean and the volunteer unoccupied for half an hour.

This page covers the formats that suit that situation, and is written for shelters, rescues and the distributors who serve them.

body.text: The no-rinse foam is the intake format

body.html:
A no-rinse foam removes three of the four expensive parts of a bath: filling a tub, waiting for a rinse, and drying. It is applied, worked in and left. For an animal too stressed for handling, or a kennel line where throughput matters more than presentation, that is the difference between a five-minute job and a thirty-minute one.

Two sizes suit different animals. The 500 mL is for larger dogs and for a full spot clean; the 300 mL is the practical size for cats and small breeds. A dedicated 200 mL paw format exists for animals coming in from outside, where the paws are the part that actually needs attention.

body.text: Where a full bath is still needed

body.html:
Intake animals arrive with more than surface dirt. Mud, fecal soiling and urine staining need a proper wash, and this is where a liquid shampoo earns its place. The multi-purpose wash is the general-purpose format — mild betaine base with camellia seed extract — and the 300 mL and 200 mL sizes cover everything from small dogs to larger animals without a bulk bottle.

The 200 mL size ships 24 to a carton, which makes it the highest-density carton in the washing range at 5.5 kg, which is worth knowing when freight is the deciding cost.

body.text: Laundry is a real line, not an afterthought

body.html:
Blankets, bedding and towels in a shelter carry the same odor as the animals, and they are frequently the reason a kennel smells even after cleaning. A detergent formulated for pet hair and pet odor, built on biological enzymes rather than ordinary surfactants, is a 1.5 kg bottle at 6 per carton.

It is a heavier carton than anything else in the range at 10.5 kg, which makes it worth including in a mixed order alongside lighter cartons so the pallet fills evenly.

body.text: Choosing between a cosmetic wash and a treatment wash

body.html:
Some animals arrive with a skin condition. That is a veterinary matter, not a grooming one, and the distinction matters for a shelter because treatment claims are regulated in most markets and must be substantiated.

The practical rule for an intake line: use a cosmetic wash as the default, and keep a claim-bearing product on the shelf for an animal a vet has already assessed. Buying the treatment format for every animal wastes money and creates a documentation problem.

body.text: Ordering, and who usually places the order

body.html:
The standard minimum is 2,000 bottles per SKU, which is more than a single shelter absorbs in a year. Shelters and rescues almost always buy through a regional distributor, an NGO procurement framework or a reseller who consolidates orders — and the format mix that works best for consolidation is the mixed-carton approach: a heavy laundry carton alongside a high-density wash carton fills a pallet far better than either alone.

If you are a distributor serving this channel, the per-SKU figures for cartons, weights and HS codes are on each product page, and minimum order, price and production time for a specific order are confirmed once the destination and quantity are known.
